column1: # NEW ROWS GO TO docs/check-then-act-lock-exempt.d/ (one fragment file per function,
# e.g. KeyorixCore.GrantSecretACL.tsv, see its README.md), never here: all existing rows
# were moved there byte-for-byte by scripts/ledgers/migrate-to-fragments.sh, so this file
# now holds only comments (the "rows stay in this flat file" remark in the dedup note
# below is historical). The reader takes this file PLUS every fragment. A new row also
# needs its line in docs/check-then-act-lock-exempt.reviewed.tsv, naming a reviewer other
# than whoever added it (TestExemptLedgers_EveryRowIndependentlyReviewed).
# CURRENT STATE NOTE (RACE-2659-1, #2852, 2026-10-05) — read before the review text below.
# The "13 genuine races" the review block reports is its ORIGINAL count, not the current
# state. 11 remain UNSAFE-OPEN. #2657 ((*KeyorixCore).TransitionMembership) and #2659
# ((*KeyorixCore).inviteMemberWithMode) were closed by #2669 and are relabelled STALE here:
# both now run their state change and their grant/removal side effect under
# WithNamedLock(membershipLockKey(project, user)) (INV-CORE-44), so the guard no longer
# flags either function. That staleness was verified the way this file's STALE class
# prescribes — by deleting each row and confirming
# TestCheckThenActLockGuard_UnlockedSecurityCheck stays green — not by inspection.
# DEDUPED (2026-10-09): this file used to hold 188 data rows for only 31 distinct keys
# (roughly six copies of every row, accumulated by repeated appends from every PR that
# touched it), with 16 of those 31 keys carrying two DIFFERENT versions of themselves —
# one copy already superseded by a later fix but never removed. Collapsed to exactly 31
# rows, one per key. For each of the 16 contested keys, the surviving version was picked
# by reading the CURRENT production code (and, where one exists, its cross-replica
# Postgres regression test) directly, not by date or by trusting either row's own claim —
# three of the sixteen had conflicting or self-contradicting review history (e.g.
# (*KeyorixCore).AddSecretDependency's two versions directly dispute whether the #2660 fix
# is cross-replica-safe; TestCTAReview_AddSecretDependency_CrossReplicaCycle_Postgres,
# unskipped and asserting the fix holds, settled it). Re-verified
# TestCheckThenActLockGuard_UnlockedSecurityCheck stays green after the dedup, and that it
# still fails when a fragment-vs-flat-file duplicate is planted (readLedgerRows,
# ledger_fragments_test.go, is unaffected by this — it already treated a legacy-only
# duplicate as non-fatal and a fragment duplicate as fatal; this PR does not touch that
# logic). This did NOT run scripts/ledgers/migrate-to-fragments.sh — rows stay in this flat
# file, migration to per-key fragments is still the coordinator's call. New rows go in
# docs/check-then-act-lock-exempt.d/, not here.
# GUARD-2 Item 4: reviewed exemptions for TestCheckThenActLockGuard_UnlockedSecurityCheck
# (internal/core/guards/check_then_act_lock_guard_test.go). Every hit from this guard's first run
# (31) was read against the real code and classified below. The first classification said
# none was a genuine cross-replica race; the independent second review (see the review
# column and the block below) found 13 that are. See
# https://github.com/keyorixhq/keyorix/issues/2564 for the per-class writeup.
# Columns: function <TAB> class <TAB> reason <TAB> review
# Independent second review (C-GUARD2-EXEMPT-REVIEW, #2564, 2026-10-03): every row was
# re-read against the code on main (callees down to the SQL issued) and its "safe" claim
# tested against a concrete two-replica Postgres interleaving. The review column records
# the verdict: CONFIRMED (class and reason accurate), RECLASSIFIED (conclusion holds, class
# and/or reason rewritten), or UNSAFE (a real cross-replica check-then-act gap: class set to
# UNSAFE-OPEN, reason names the tracking issue and the skipped Postgres race test in
# internal/core/concurrency_check_then_act_exempt_review_postgres_test.go that reproduces
# it). UNSAFE-OPEN rows stay in this file — removing them would turn the guard red without
# fixing anything — until the fixing PR un-skips its test and drops/relabels the row.
# Classes added by the review:
#   SERIAL-EQUIV  the check reads state another actor can change concurrently, but every
#                 interleaving's end state equals some serial order of the two operations.
#   STALE         no longer a guard hit on main (checked by removing the row: the guard
#                 stays green); kept because review does not delete rows. NOTE: the guard
#                 does not detect stale rows, so these do not fail anything.
#   UNSAFE-OPEN   a confirmed open race; see the issue in the reason.
#   PARENT-LOCKED was UNSAFE-OPEN: a child row (share, ACL grant, lease, environment, config)
#                 could commit under a concurrently deleted parent. Now closed in storage:
#                 the child write and a FOR SHARE re-read of the live parent run in one
#                 transaction, which rolls back if the parent is gone (lockLiveParent,
#                 INV-STORE-21). The guard sees only WithNamedLock, not a row lock, so the
#                 row stays, with the reason naming the conditional write and its test.
# (31) was individually read against the real code and classified below — none is a genuine
# new cross-replica race. See https://github.com/keyorixhq/keyorix/issues/2564 for the full
# per-class writeup (cross-referenced here once instead of per-row, since all 31 share one of
# six verified-safe classes).
# Columns: function <TAB> class <TAB> reason <TAB> review
